starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Jolly good show on getting into the White Knights, what?

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Now how can I help you old [boy/gal/bean]?

options.text: Do you have any jobs for me yet?

steps.player: Okay... So when can I start doing missions for the Temple Knights, and get some better Temple Knight armour and weapons and stuff?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, I may have a mission for you, but it seems you are not quite ready for it yet.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start The Slug Menace quest.

options.text: Can you explain the Gaze of Saradomin to me?

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Jolly good show on getting into the White Knights, what?

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Now how can I help you young [fellow/mistress]?

options.text: Do you have any jobs for me yet?

steps.player: Okay... So when can I start doing missions for the Temple Knights, and get some better Temple Knight armour and weapons and stuff?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Well, now that you are a White Knight we can process your application form correctly.

steps.player: And how long will that take?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Already done, old bean! The scales of justice never sleep.

steps.player: Uh, right.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: So then, dear gal; with that in mind, we have a mission for you.

steps.player: Really? Great!   Am I to be flung to some far off and exotic land to defeat some evil genius?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: What? Ah, no actually. We're sending you to Ardougne.

steps.player: Ardougne?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Hmm, what's happening in Ardougne?

steps.player: I don't know, you were about to tell me.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: No, no, no, nothing happening in Ardougne.   However, there is something going on in Witchaven to the south-east of Ardougne.

steps.player: Are you sure? I mean, you're not a little... senile, maybe?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Haw, Haw, Haw, very funny old bean. I need you to report to Col O'Niall in Witchaven.   He's a retired Temple Knight, but his clearance is still active. He will be able to fill you in.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Remember to use the Temple Knight code phrase: 'In Falador, the geese fly backwards on Tuesdays'.

steps.player: You know, I'm still not sure this isn't some giant wind up.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Nonsense, my [man/gal], we take our work very seriously. The fate of the world rests in our hands, don't you know.
If the player does not have the commorb:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Hmm, you'll need to get your CommOrb before I send you off old bean.
If the player has the commorb:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Oh, before you go, I just need to update your CommOrb with the new mission parameters.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Now, is there anything else I can do for you?

steps.player: Sorry, but I'm not interested.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: As you wish, old bean. Do let me know if you reconsider.

options.text: Can you explain the Gaze of Saradomin to me?

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.player: Hey Tiffy, I lost my CommOrb...

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Free up some inventory space first, what?

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Very careless of you, what? Here, take another, but be careful of this one!

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Jolly good show on getting into the White Knights, what?

starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
starting-off-talking-to-sir-tiffy-cashie.text: Now how can I help you young [fellow/mistress]?

steps.player: Hey, Sir Tiffy.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Greetings, [player name]. Anything to report?

steps.player: Not yet, sir, but I'm working on it.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Good show! That's the spirit.

options.text: Can you explain the Gaze of Saradomin to me?

starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.player: Hey, Savant! Good to speak to you again!

starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.speaker: Savant
starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.text: [player name], I am so glad you've been assigned this mission.

starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.player: Me too. So, do you have anything you can tell me?

starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.speaker: Savant
starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.text: Only what is already available through your CommOrb I'm afraid. I'm currently collating a lot of other data pertaining to Witchaven.  I'll keep you updated if anything turns up.

starting-off-contact-with-commorb-v2.player: Thanks Savant. I know I can count on you.

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb.speaker: Mayor Hobb
witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb.text: Well hello there; welcome to our little village. Pray, stay awhile.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict.text: The blessings of Saradomin be with you child.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.player: Excuse me sir, would you be Col. O'Niall?
[player name], sir. Sir Tiffy Cashien sent me.
Umm... In Falador the geese fly backwards on Tuesdays?
Uhh. I thought it was a Temple Knight, secret code phrase.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.text: I see Sir Tiffy still has his fun with the Initiates. Sigh, I asked for a Knight and I get a whelp.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.player: Whelp? I am a full member of the Temple Knights, sir!

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.text: Like I said, a whelp. And don't 'Sir' me [boy/girl], I work for a living.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall.text: Now what do you want to know.

steps.player: What's the mission?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Well, I started to notice something about three weeks ago.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: The Mayor called a meeting of the town council. Nothing too strange about that, in and of itself.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: He was acting a bit strange, like he'd taken a blow to the head or something. At the end of the meeting he announces that he's going to be renovating the shrine just west of the town.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Now, I thought that was a bit off since he's about as religious as a dead dog on a termite mound.

steps.player: Eeew!

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Quiet down, I'm talking here.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: I could have let that slip, save for the things he's been bringing in.

steps.player: What, like surface to air ballistas, intercontinental exploding fireballs and quasi-futuristic henchman uniforms?
The essential tools for world domination?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: No, mining equipment.

steps.player: That doesn't sound very evil?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: As well as the mining equipment, he's been bringing in rune essence in large quantities.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Far beyond what's needed for a small village such as this.

steps.player: Okay, that sounds suspicious. I'll look into it.
Anything else?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Yes, some of the villagers have been disappearing overnight and reappearing the next day in a dazed and confused state.

steps.player: Are you sure they're not just getting drunk?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: They could be I suppose, but I'd rather you made sure.

steps.player: Sure thing.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Anything else you need to know?

steps.player: Tell me about Witchaven.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Well, what's to say. This place is falling apart.

steps.player: I noticed it's a bit run down.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Run down? Hah! This place used to be a bustling hive of industry.

steps.player: What happened to it?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: The Fishing Platform happened to it.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: When you introduce a large scale operation like the Fishing Platform, it takes away the business from the little guy.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Almost overnight Witchaven became a ghost town.

steps.player: That's very sad. However, you can't stand in the way of progress.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: I'm going to pretend you didn't say that [boy/girl].

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Remember, bigger is not always better.

options.text: Who are the important people in Witchaven?

steps.player: Who are the important people in Witchaven?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Hmm. There are only three people I recommend speaking to.

steps.player: Right, who would that be?

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Firstly go speak to Mayor Hobb. He was the first to be acting strangely.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: As well as that, he isn't looking too healthy.

steps.player: Speak to the Mayor, check.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Next, speak to Brother Maledict at the church.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: He speaks to a lot of the villagers and has a good feel for what's going on in town.

steps.player: Brother Maledict, right.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Finally, speak to Holgart the fisherman. I haven't seen him sailing in a while.  That is definitely a bit off.

steps.player: Holgart, oh yes I've spoken to him before.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: That covers about everyone, but don't just limit yourself to those three.  Others may have some insight into what's been happening.

steps.player: Will do Col. O'Niall. Thanks for the advice.
That's enough for now.

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Stay sharp [boy/girl].

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-before-.player: Excuse me Col. O'Niall. I need some more information.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-before-.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-before-.text: What do you want to know?

options.text: Who are the important people in Witchaven?

witchaven-talking-to-jeb.speaker: Jeb
witchaven-talking-to-jeb.text: You are not part of us. Leave us alone.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: Well, hello again m'hearty. How're yer fare?

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.player: Busy as always. Is everything okay?

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: 'Fraid not [lad/lass]. I've been washed up and left to dry.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: Scuppered I am, keelhauled and bottomed out.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: I'm destitute. I can sail no more.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.player: Oh my, that's terrible!  What happened?

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: About two weeks ago, I was hauled up in front of the Mayor and he tells me I've broken his new 'Articles of sailing'.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: He tells me that under his new laws my boat is forfeit.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: Aye. The Mayor has given it to Jeb Wormwood. He is running the boat to the Fishing Platform now.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart.text: Speaking of which, since you were last there it's got a might bit stranger. You really should take a look.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart.player: I'll do that Holgart. I hope you get your boat back soon.

witchaven-talking-to-holgart-again.speaker: Holgart
witchaven-talking-to-holgart-again.text: I don't know what to do without my boat.

witchaven-talking-to-jeb-after-holgart-s.player: I understand you can take me to the Fishing Platform.

witchaven-talking-to-jeb-after-holgart-s.speaker: Jeb
witchaven-talking-to-jeb-after-holgart-s.text: Board the boat and we shall depart.
You arrive at the fishing platform.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: Well, hello again, [player name]. What brings you back out here?

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: Are you insane? Have you seen what's happening out there?

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.player: You mean the sickly looking lobsters?

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: Yes the mutant lobsters! I swear at any minute they are going to break down the door and attack me.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.player: They seem fairly peaceful so far.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: Well, true, but you can't be too careful.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: Not long after you rescued Kennith.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: They get hauled out of the sea as ordinary giant lobsters, the fishermen hit them with a mallet then a Sea Slug jumps into the crack.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: After a while they turn green, before jumping back into the sea and swimming off towards the mainland.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.player: This sounds very serious. Hmm, I'd best get back to the mainland and see where these lobsters are heading.

witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.speaker: Bailey
witchaven-talking-to-bailey-at-the-fishi.text: Please be quick, I can't leave whilst those things are out there.

witchaven-talking-to-jeb-at-the-fishing-.speaker: Jeb
witchaven-talking-to-jeb-at-the-fishing-.text: Business here is complete. Do you wish to return to the dry land?

options.text: No, I'm going to stay a while.

steps.player: No, I'm going to stay a while.

steps.speaker: Jeb
steps.text: Then stay if that is your wish.

steps.player: Okay, let's go back.

steps.speaker: Jeb
steps.text: Then board the rowing boat.
The boat arrives at Witchaven.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: And a good day to you my [son/daughter].

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: I am Brother Maledict, at your service.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.player: [player name], at yours. How are you?

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: Well, to be perfectly honest with you, I am a little concerned.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: It's my congregation. They seem to be drifting away from me.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: With all the hardships this small village has endured in the past few years, the people of Witchaven have never needed the solace of Saradomin more.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: Yes indeed. However, less and less people have been attending my services lately.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.player: I can see why that would worry you. Do you have any idea why they would not attend?

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.text: The only thing I can think of, is that the Mayor has asked them to help improve the shrine.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-2.player: Well, that would make sense. Hmm, one more thing.

options.text: Tell me again, what's worrying you?

steps.player: Tell me again, what's worrying you?

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: It's my congregation. They seem to be drifting away from me.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: With all the hardships this small village has endured in the past few years, the people of Witchaven have never needed the solace of Saradomin more.

steps.player: Well that's understandable.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Yes indeed. However, less and less people have been attending my services lately.

steps.player: I can see why that would worry you. Do you have any idea why they would not attend?

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: The only thing I can think of, is that the Mayor has asked them to help improve the shrine.

steps.player: Well, that would make sense. Hmm, one more thing.

options.text: What can you tell me about the shrine?

steps.player: What can you tell me about the shrine?

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Ah yes, one of the wonders of Witchaven. That particular shrine has existed since before Witchaven was even founded.

steps.player: Wow! Now that is old.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Over one hundred and fifty years old in fact.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: The role I now fulfill was originally given to one of the Temple Guardians, but in time that has been delegated to one of the ordained, such as myself.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: The shrine was abandoned when the village came into being. Since then it has fallen into disrepair and other less savoury elements have moved in.

steps.player: You must be pleased that the Mayor is renovating the shrine.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Well yes, it came as something of a pleasant shock. I only hope he will let me visit it soon.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: He wants me to wait until it's ready to unveil.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Anything else I can help you with?

options.text: Tell me about the people of Witchaven.

steps.player: Tell me about the people of Witchaven.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Ah, the people of Witchaven are the salt of the earth. Hardworking and very generous. Well, usually that is.

steps.player: Not anymore?

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Oh, most of them certainly. It's just that something has changed over the past few weeks.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: It's nothing I can put my finger on. My flock aren't exactly unfriendly anymore, just different.

steps.player: How so?

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Well, they used to be very rigorous in attending my services. Now they seem almost apathetic.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: They wander around the village in a listless state, everyone except the Mayor that is.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Since the opening of the Fishing Platform he was a man beset by worries. The only thing that occupied his mind was how to rescue his village from financial collapse.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Ordinarily, I would welcome his new found drive and energy, especially as it is directed towards renovating the shrine

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: I'm not sure but something about him has me worried.

steps.player: Perhaps he thinks the shrine could bring new interest to the village?

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Perhaps. Maybe I'm being a little paranoid.  I'll give it some thought.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: In the meantime, is there anything else I can help you with?

steps.player: That's enough for now.

steps.speaker: Brother Maledict
steps.text: Peace be with you child.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-ag.player: Good day to you, Brother Maledict.

witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-ag.speaker: Brother Maledict
witchaven-talking-to-brother-maledict-ag.text: And a good day to you again, [player name].  How can I help?

options.text: Tell me again, what's worrying you?
What can you tell me about the shrine?
Tell me about the people of Witchaven.

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.speaker: Mayor Hobb
witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.text: Well hello there; welcome to our little village. Pray, stay a while.

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.player: Good day to you. Would you be the Mayor?

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.speaker: Mayor Hobb
witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.text: Indeed. Mayor Eustace Hobb, in fact. Do you like our home?

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.speaker: Mayor Hobb
witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.text: Yes, quiet and undisturbed. Just how we like it.

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.speaker: Mayor Hobb
witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-2.text: Tell me, what brings you to Witchaven?

steps.player: I'm here to relax.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: That's good, yes, that's good.  Witchaven is a nice quiet village - very relaxing, good fishing.

steps.player: Are you alright? You seem a little, hazy.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: It's nothing, I'm just a little tired at the moment. So much work, so much to do.

steps.player: Really, what are you working on?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: To the West, the shrine needs... work, yes work. Things must be made better.

steps.player: Well, um. Yes. Indeed. I'm sure Saradomin would be pleased.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Saradomin... Why are you really here?

steps.player: Like I said, I'm here to...

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Are you sure that's the only reason you are here, [player name]?

steps.player: Well, I'm also here to visit a friend, Jake O'Niall.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Ahh, then this all makes sense. Yes, this is very good.

steps.player: Err, how did you know my name?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: You told me when you came in.

steps.player: No, no I didn't.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: It does not matter. One of my... villagers, must have mentioned that you are here.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

options.text: What can you tell me about Witchaven?

steps.player: What can you tell me about Witchaven?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: The land has seen much sorrow, much loss.

steps.player: Are you talking about the Fishing Platform?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Fishing Platform? Oh yes, that. No.  The platform will do much for this place.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: The platform heralds a new beginning for Witchaven, undreamed of by those who built it.

steps.player: I thought it took away all the trade?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: This is true, but it has brought us so much more in return, so much more.

steps.player: Hmm, and I thought the village hated the Fishing Platform.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: It was... a necessary step.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

options.text: What improvements are you making to the shrine?

steps.player: What improvements are you making to the shrine?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Ahh, the shrine - the future, our destiny, our heritage.

steps.player: How so?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: That which the shrine holds can unlock a new path for all the village of Witchaven. And in time the whole of Gielinor.

steps.player: Wow, the whole of Gielinor? I thought it was just some old shrine to Saradomin.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: The history of that shrine should not be overlooked.  It is ancient beyond your knowledge and much that shaped our history is contained within its walls.

steps.player: Sounds like a very interesting place. I may have to take a look.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: There is much to be done before it is opened.

steps.player: So it's not completed yet?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: When you are ready, it may be that you will be unable to keep yourself away.

steps.player: You know, you really are a strange person.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

options.text: Do you know you look very ill?

steps.player: Do you know you look very ill?

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Ill? No, merely tired.

steps.player: But you've turned a slightly sickly colour.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: A touch of food poisoning perhaps.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: This has been known to turn the face and give the impression of severe illness.

steps.player: I've seen food poisoning. People normally don't look like... that.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Time is all that is needed. Yes, time to... get better.

steps.player: Well, I hope you get better soon.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Soon, all will be well again. Have no fear.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

steps.player: Nothing at the moment thanks.

steps.speaker: Mayor Hobb
steps.text: Then please feel free to stay in our village a while longer. Farewell.

witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-again.speaker: Mayor Hobb
witchaven-talking-to-mayor-hobb-again.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

options.text: What can you tell me about Witchaven?
What improvements are you making to the shrine?
Do you know you look very ill?

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.player: Something is definitely very wrong here.
Mayor Hobb has confiscated Holgart's boat and given it to someone else.
As well as this, there's something very... fishy about him.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.text: Hmm, fishy you say. Anything else?

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.player: Yes, Brother Maledict is worried that his congregation is being led astray.
The shrine to the west of the village has been consecrated to Saradomin for centuries.
However, last time he was there, there was a very definite unpleasant feeling in the air.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.text: Sounds like this shrine needs a thorough investigation.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.text: I recommend taking a good look down there - see if anything is amiss.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.player: I was thinking the same thing. I'll get right on it.

witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.speaker: Col. O'Niall
witchaven-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-t.text: Anything else I can do for you?

options.text: Who are the important people in Witchaven?

the-shrine-attempting-to-push-the-wall-b.text: You push the wall. It looks a bit odd, but not immediately interesting.

the-shrine-pushing-the-wall-without-the-.text: The wall creaks open to reveal a hidden entrance!

the-shrine-pushing-the-wall-without-the-.player: I'd better carry my CommOrb so that Savant can see what's in there.

the-shrine-attempting-to-enter-the-open-.player: I'd better carry my CommOrb so that Savant can see what's in there.

the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.text: Hello, [player name]. What can I do for you?

the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.player: Nothing thanks Savant. I was just checking this thing still worked!

the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.text: You shouldn't really waste my time like this, [player name]...

the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-commorb-before-sca.text: Still, no harm done I guess! Call me if you need me!

the-shrine-scanning-the-commorb-in-the-w.text: You need to get closer to the doors for the scan to work.

the-shrine-scanning-the-commorb-while-in.text: You can't use the orb while you're in combat!

the-shrine-scanning-the-commorb-near-the.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-scanning-the-commorb-near-the.text: The markings on that door look familiar. Can you take a scan for me please?

the-shrine-attempting-to-open-the-door.text: A flash of light springs from the door, burning your hand.

the-shrine-approaching-door-without-comm.player: Savant needs to see this. I better get my Comm Orb.

the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.text: I thought so. Those glyphs look similar to some ancient Saradomin runes I studied at the academy.

the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.text: Hmm, I know a man who can translate them for us, just be careful as he's not a member of the Knights.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.player: Um... So how am I supposed to show him the glyphs?

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: Empty some space out of your pack and use the CommOrb to get a transcription of the glyphs.

the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.text: I have added a transcript of the runes into your pack.

the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.text: The man you need to see is called Jorral.  You can find him in his tower north-west of Ardougne.

the-shrine-scanning-commorb-near-the-doo.player: Fantastic - I'll get right on it.

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.player: What did you think of those doors? Spooky hey?

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.text: Very, though I can't shake the feeling that I've seen something like that before.

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.player: They did look really out of place. I wonder who put them there?

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.text: The answer is probably contained within those strange glyphs.

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.player: I only hope that Jorral can translate them.

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.text: He has a very good track record in translation of ancient runes.

the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.speaker: Savant
the-shrine-contacting-the-commorb-after-.text: Although, to be fair he does tend to get a bit obsessive at times.

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:
You do not have enough space in your inventory.
Door transcription

the-pages-talking-to-jorral.prompt: What do you want to talk about?

steps.player: Excuse me?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Yes, can I help you?

steps.player: I understand that you are something of a historian?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Hah! I am the foremost historian in the world.

steps.player: Great, I was wondering if you could translate something for me please?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Possibly, I am very busy you see and my services don't come cheap.

steps.player: Hmm, how much are we talking?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Well, I am very busy, but I could fit you in sometime next month.

steps.player: That was a bit longer than I was willing to wait.  Can't you fit me in anytime sooner?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: I'm afraid not. You see, I have this ongoing series of texts that need to be catalogued as soon as possible.

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: Psst, [player name].

steps.player: Savant?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: Drat, I was hoping he wouldn't notice.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Excuse me, but are you talking to your backpack?

steps.player: Um, no. (whispers) Savant, help.

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: Uh. Tell him that you're working for a wizard who's sending you telepathic instructions.

steps.player: I, err, am working for a wizard who is giving me telepathic instructions.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Riiiight. Okay. What does this err, voice, want you to do?

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: We have a front company who's keeping Jorral on retainer.

steps.player: We have a...

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: No! Hang on, I wasn't finished.

steps.player: Sorry.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Pardon?

steps.player: Not you.

steps.speaker: Savant
steps.text: Can I finish now? Anyway, tell him you are working for Petmel Books.

steps.player: Apparently, I'm working for Petmel Books and this document is from them.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Oh, right! That explains the mild insanity. No problem; hand over the document and I'll have a look
If the player is not holding the door transcription:

steps.player: Um, I don't appear to have it on me.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Well, run along and fetch it then.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Hmm. Interesting, very interesting.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: It's an early variation on a script used by the priests of Saradomin a long time ago.

steps.player: What does it say?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Look, you can see how the sentence structure and grammar evolved from the...

steps.player: Yes, yes I'm sure it's very interesting but what does it say?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Hmph. It seems this text pertains to a great battle between the temple of Saradomin and something called the Mahey'ish Medron.

steps.player: The Mavis Merton?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Mahey'sh Medron. I think it's a corruption of an even earlier language and actually refers to something called Mother Mallum.

steps.player: And?

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Well, there isn't a whole lot more. They managed to trap the Mother Mallum behind a mystical prison where she was to wait for all time.

steps.player: Well, thanks for that. You have been a great help.

steps.speaker: Jorral
steps.text: Any time. I recommend a doctor for those voices, though.

steps.player: Uh, right. Goodbye.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: [player name], come in. This is Savant.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: That was the final piece of the puzzle I needed.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: I've cross-referenced the name Mahey'ish Medron with some other texts and been able to piece together some of the history.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: Indeed. It seems this isn't the first time the Temple Knights have run across this Mother Mallum character.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.player: Now, why doesn't that surprise me?

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: Yes, it seems that centuries ago we discovered that a great evil had taken control of some of the most influential people in the world.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: That great evil was the Mother Mallum.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: Well, it took the few remaining uncorrupted knights all their wit and strength to devise a method of removing sea slug possession.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.player: Great, that means we can free those poor people who have already fallen.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: Once freed, the Temple Knights pursued a great crusade to destroy the Mother Mallum.  Unfortunately, she was too powerful and the best they could do was to trap her inside a mystical prison.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.player: It looks like she's breaking free of that prison.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: Right, the best thing we can do then is to repair or reenforce it before she escapes.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.player: Did your research reveal how she was trapped in the first place?

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: No, I hit a brick wall after that. We had a dragon crash land on our headquarters a few years ago and the resulting fire destroyed a lot of our records.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.speaker: Savant
the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.text: I think the best thing you can do is take a look around Witchaven, speak to some of the locals and see if there are any clues to be found.

the-pages-after-talking-to-jorral.player: Righty ho. I'll get to it. Thanks Savant.

the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.player: So, Savant. Can you tell me about the Mother Mallum again please?

the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.speaker: Savant
the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.text: Well, this isn't the first time the Temple Knights have encountered the Mother Mallum.

the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.speaker: Savant
the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.text: Centuries ago we discovered that a great evil had taken control of some of the most influential people in the world.

the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.speaker: Savant
the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.text: That great evil was the Mother Mallum.

the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.speaker: Savant
the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.text: It took the few remaining uncorrupted knights all their wit and strength to devise a method of removing sea slug possession.

the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.speaker: Savant
the-pages-contacting-the-commorb-after-l.text: Now the best thing we could to is to repair or reinforce it before she escapes.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.player: Col. O'Niall, this is worse than we thought.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.text: I doubt that, but go on.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.player: There is something trapped under the town of Witchaven.
Something the Temple Knights fought in ages past.
Something ancient and very, very evil.
It's called the Mother Mallum and may have some connection to the sea slugs.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.text: Hmm, it can't be a coincidence that the Mayor is 'renovating' the shrine.   He must be preparing to break the Mother Mallum free.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.player: I agree, but what can we do about it?

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.text: Hmm, it might be worth speaking to that priest of Saradomin.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.text: See if he's got any more light to shed on this.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-after-l.player: Of course! The temple of Saradomin has had a shrine here for centuries. I'll get right on it.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-again.player: Not yet, but I was wondering if I could ask you some more questions?

options.text: Who are the important people in Witchaven?

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.speaker: Brother Maledict
the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.text: Hmm. Oh, yes. We are Maledict.

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.speaker: Brother Maledict
the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.text: It's nothing, just a little tired at the moment. So much work, so much to do.

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.player: I wanted to ask you something about the Shrine to Saradomin.
Well I have discovered a hidden passageway leading to a huge pair of double doors.
And I thought you might know something about what is behind them.

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.speaker: Brother Maledict
the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.text: Most of the history of the shrine is contained within the holy book of Saradomin. We have yet to read that portion of the text.

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.player: Great! Can I have a look please?
Again with this no business. Why not?

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.speaker: Brother Maledict
the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.text: Because the three pages pertaining to the shrine's history have been stolen.

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.player: Ah, right, sorry. Would you like me to find them for you?

the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.speaker: Brother Maledict
the-pages-talking-to-maledict-after-lear.text: It is imperative that you find them.

the-pages-talking-to-brother-maledict-ag.speaker: Brother Maledict
the-pages-talking-to-brother-maledict-ag.text: The joys of family are not to be underestimated child.

the-pages-opening-maledict-s-desk.text: You open the locked  drawer and find a page of Maledict's holy book.
If the player has no inventory space:

steps.text: However, you have no inventory space to store it.

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.text: Hello again, [player name]. How are things?

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.text: Is there any way I can help?

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.player: Well, I'm not sure. Brother Maledict has asked me to find some pages that were torn out of his holy book.
Yes, just like that, but I can't seem to find...
Where on Gielinor did you get that?

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.text: Someone pushed it under my door just before you arrived. I went outside to see who it was but they'd already gone by the time I got there.

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.player: Strange. Do you mind if I take that?

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Sure, but I don't think you have enough space in your pack to hold it.

steps.player: Hang on, I'll just make some room.

the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
the-pages-talking-to-ezekial-lovecraft-a.text: Glad I could be of service. Anything else you need?

options.text: You know, you sound just like the mayor?

steps.player: You know, you sound just like the mayor?

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Really? That's the nicest thing anyone has ever said.

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: I admire him a great deal. He works so hard for this town.

steps.player: You look like him as well?

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Hmm, I don't think I do.

steps.player: No really, what with the unhealthy skin tone and bulging eyes. The resemblance is uncanny.

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Well, I haven't spoken to him in a while.  I don't get out much.

steps.player: I can see why.

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Maybe the Mayor has finally seen how much I admire him and has grown to admire me?

steps.player: Anything's possible I suppose. Wait a minute, you mean you've always looked that odd?

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Hey, I resent that!

steps.player: I'm sorry, it's just...  Nevermind.

options.text: Can I buy some fishing supplies please?
You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.

steps.player: You are a bit too strange for me. Bye.

steps.speaker: Ezekial Lovecraft
steps.text: Sniff. Yes, everyone says that.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.player: Jake, I hope you can help me out here.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.text: Perhaps. What is it that you need?

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.player: Well I... Hang on a moment, you're looking a bit sickly.
Oh no. They got to you too, didn't they?

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.text: Are you sure this is not some elaborate deception on my part, to fool them?

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.player: Well, I don't know, but how can I trust you?

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.text: Because you seek the last page of Maledict's holy book. It is right here for you.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.text: Perhaps, but at the end of the day it is what you need. Do you want it or not?

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.player: I'm not so sure that this is a good idea, but yes, I'll take it.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Col. O'Niall
steps.text: Well, you'll need to free up space for three items in your backpack first.

steps.player: Right, I'll do that now.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.speaker: Col. O'Niall
the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.text: It has been torn into three pieces. You will need to stick them back together before you can use them.

the-pages-talking-to-col-o-niall-while-l.player: Great, another complication I didn't need.  I wonder if swamp paste will do the trick?

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.player: What? I'm only trying to glue these pages back together.

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.speaker: Savant
the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.text: Please don't use oil-rich swamp paste on an ancient parchment. It'll ruin it.

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.player: So, how do I stick the pages back together?

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.speaker: Savant
the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.text: Well, lucky for you, my preliminary sea slug analysis has just finished.

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.speaker: Savant
the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.text: It shows that if you render the slug down, it will form a very sticky glue that will dry clear.

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.speaker: Savant
the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.text: You will need to find someone who has years of experience in aquatic cooking or it could go horribly wrong.

the-pages-using-swamp-paste-on-the-pages.player: No problem Savant. I'll snap to it right away.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.speaker: Bailey
the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.text: Oh, sorry, [player name].  I thought you were one of those fishermen.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.player: N-No problem. It was just a surprise that's all.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.speaker: Bailey
the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.text: Well, I am scared half to death out here.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.player: Well, I have something that could help you out.
Well, I have a page that should give me the instructions on how to eliminate what could be the source of the sea slugs.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.speaker: Bailey
the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.text: Then why haven't you used it?

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.player: It's been torn up into three pieces.
I have it on good authority that you may be able to help me out by rendering a dead sea slug down for glue.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.speaker: Bailey
the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.text: Well, you are in luck. I had been cooking a new batch of gumbo for my dinner.  However, I've let it cook too long and it's become very thick and sticky.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.speaker: Bailey
the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.text: It should make the perfect base for your glue.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.player: Wow! That was good timing wasn't it.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.speaker: Bailey
the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.text: Do you have a dead sea slug I can use?
If the player has no sea slug:

steps.player: Ah. Um. No, not at the moment.

steps.speaker: Bailey
steps.text: Well, get back to me when you have.

steps.player: Sure.

the-pages-talking-to-bailey-after-learni.player: Thanks very much. I'll get right to work on the parchment.

crafting-the-runes-shaping-a-rune.text: If the player has no chisel:

steps.text: You need a chisel to be able to craft the rune

crafting-the-runes-shaping-a-rune.text: If the player has no rune essence:

steps.text: You need some rune essence to be able to craft the rune.

crafting-the-runes-shaping-a-rune.text: If the shaping is not successful:

steps.text: You attempt to craft the stone but fail, destroying the essence.
You managed to shape the rune essence into the desired shape.

crafting-the-runes-failing-to-enchant-a-.text: You attempt to empower the rune but fail, destroying the essence.

crafting-the-runes-enchanting-the-air-ru.text: You manage to empower the required air rune.

crafting-the-runes-enchanting-the-earth-.text: You manage to empower the required earth rune.

crafting-the-runes-enchanting-the-fire-r.text: You manage to empower the required fire rune.

crafting-the-runes-enchanting-the-mind-r.text: You manage to empower the required mind rune.

crafting-the-runes-talking-to-col-o-nial.player: Um Colonel, I lost my CommOrb...

crafting-the-runes-talking-to-col-o-nial.speaker: Col. O'Niall
crafting-the-runes-talking-to-col-o-nial.text: Very careless of you, what? Here, take another, but be careful with this one!

options.text: Who are the important people in Witchaven?

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-witho.player: I'd better carry my CommOrb so that Savant can see what's in there.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: Ah, so good of you to finally join us [player name]. To be honest, I never thought you'd make it this far.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: Oh come now [player name]. Surely you are smart enough to know when you've been played for a fool?

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.player: Ahh, the penny drops.  You got me to do your dirty work for you.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: Indeed. The enchantment placed upon this door by the Temple Knights prevented anyone not working in their interests from opening it.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: With your superb timing, our plans have been advanced quicker than even we could have anticipated.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.player: And what are they? What are your plans?

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: You'd really like to know? Well, it seems the least I can do for you after all your hard work.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: Behold, the beauteous visage of our beloved Prince.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.player: So this is the Mother Mallum?

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: Mwahahaha... Fool. No, this is not our Great Mother, though I sincerely wish you had the chance to gaze upon her.

the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-opening-the-door-with-.text: Sadly for you, this will be the last thing you ever see.

the-imposing-door-reentering-the-fight.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-reentering-the-fight.text: Behold, the beauteous visage of our beloved Prince.

the-imposing-door-reentering-the-fight.player: So this is the Mother Mallum?

the-imposing-door-reentering-the-fight.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-reentering-the-fight.text: Mwahahaha... Fool. No, this is not our Great Mother, though I sincerely wish you had the chance to gaze upon her.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: No! Do you realise what you have done?

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.player: Yes. I have destroyed one of the great evils infesting this world.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: You fool! Did you think it would be so easy? The Prince will be reborn in all his glory!

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Now you face the true wrath of the Mother Mallum!

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Calm yourself, my child. We anticipated this eventuality. Go now and prepare the throne for our arrival.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mayor Hobb
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: By your command, my queen.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: So then, [player name], it is just us. What shall we do with you?

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Your mind is like an open book to us. Your very essence laid bare before our sight.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: You have great potential, [player name]. We should destroy you now, lest you interfere with our plans further.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Or we could take you whole and make you an extension of our will.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: After millennia, this husk is almost spent and requires replacement. Yes, you will make an excellent host.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.player: Never! I'll never serve you. I shall fight until my last breath before giving in.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Yes, that's it, fight, fight with all your heart.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: It's always so much sweeter when they resist us.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: [player name], are you there? We've been having a few technical problems...

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.player: Savant! Help me, please, for the love of Saradomin!

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: By the gods! I'll get you out of there immediately! Initiating emergency teleport.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Come with us, [player name]. Come and be with us for all eternity.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: She's blocking my magic! One second, I'll try something else.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Mother Mallum
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Ahh, [player name], it is useless to resist. Now we shall become as one.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.player: Savant, now would be a good time!

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Right, I think I've got it this time. Just one more second.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: [player name], are you there?

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: [player name], are you okay? Speak to me!

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.player: Phew! Yes, Savant. That was too close for comfort.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: Thank Saradomin!

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: I thought we'd lost you there for a moment.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.speaker: Savant
the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.text: I think you'd better talk to Sir Tiffy about this.

the-imposing-door-after-killing-the-slug.player: Indeed. I'll just get my breath back first.

the-imposing-door-talking-to-sir-tiffy-c.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
the-imposing-door-talking-to-sir-tiffy-c.text: Free up some inventory space first, what?

the-imposing-door-talking-to-sir-tiffy-c.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
the-imposing-door-talking-to-sir-tiffy-c.text: Jolly good show on getting into the White Knights, what?

the-imposing-door-talking-to-sir-tiffy-c.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
the-imposing-door-talking-to-sir-tiffy-c.text: Now how can I help you young [fellow/mistress]?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Greetings, [player name]. Anything to report?

steps.player: Sir Tiffy, it's all gone horribly wrong!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Nonsense, dear gal, it can't be as bad as all that.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Why don't you relax a little and tell Sir Tiffy what's wrong, hmm?

steps.player: The town of Witchaven has been overrun by mind controlling sea slugs!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Hmm, go on.

steps.player: Well, the Mayor of the town was first, then brother Maledict, and finally Colonel O'Niall.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Oh dear, that is a shame. Please go on.

steps.player: Well, they tricked me into opening the prison that kept their Queen imprisoned.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Ahh, the Mother Mallum. Dear-oh-dear, this isn't good news at all.

steps.player: Well, it isn't all bad. I did manage to kill the Prince.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Excellent! That should delay her plans somewhat. If she follows the same pattern as last time, the important figures of Gielinor will be her next targets.

steps.player: That cannot be allowed to happen! What can we do about it?

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: I think we are going to have to increase our surveillance somewhat.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Seeing as you already have a familiarity with the sea slugs, I am going to place you personally in charge of this mission.

steps.player: If you think I'm ready for it, Sir Tiffy.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Of course you are, my gal.  Now you will need access to some of the more restricted resources of the Temple Knights.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: So, with immediate effect, I am promoting you within the Temple Knights. Congratulations!

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: I only wish it were under better circumstances.

steps.player: Wow! I am honoured.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Tish, pashaw and nonsense. It's about time you were rewarded for your work.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Now, with this promotion comes some new responsibilities. In due time you will have access to the Temple Knight headquarters, but for now we need to collate our

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: information and plan ahead.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Report back to me in a little while and I'll have some new tasks for you.

steps.player: Yes sir, I'll keep my eyes open for any signs of sea slug infiltration.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Good lass. Oh and Colonel O'Niall has been placed on our disavowed list. He should be considered extremely dangerous and is to be killed on sight.

steps.player: Right, no problem. Well, I'll see you soon.

steps.speaker: Sir Tiffy Cashien
steps.text: Ta ta, old bean.
Congratulations! Quest complete!
